---
title: Home
---

What if the key to running faster and jumping higher was hidden in just a few months of explosive training?

This project investigates how plyometric jump training relates to jump performance in youth soccer players, and whether results differ by biological maturity. Published research will help guide a progressive six-month training plan.

**Research question:** How does 12 weeks of plyometric jump training affect countermovement jump height in youth male soccer players, and does the change differ before and after peak height velocity (PHV)?

## Featured result: countermovement jump

Each point shows the group mean of each athlete's average across three jump trials. PHV groups and control/PJT groups are shown separately.
